memory_update.text: WEST is the highest-quality direct public-market fit for the private-label coffee, tea, extracts, and beverage-solutions node because it explicitly serves foodservice, restaurant, convenience, hospitality, CPG, and private-label/RTD extract use cases.

FARM is a direct but highly speculative micro-cap route-service coffee/tea/foodservice supplier; keep only if later layers verify DSD economics, customer retention, liquidity, and debt/covenant safety.
JVA is a micro-cap speculative-shadow candidate for regional private-label and foodservice coffee exposure; evidence must verify materiality of foodservice/private-label revenue and customer quality.
KDP should be used as a reference benchmark for scaled away-from-home coffee systems, K-Cup manufacturing, and restaurant fountain relationships, not as the underfollowed discovery target.

TreeHouse Foods was historically relevant through the Farmer Brothers coffee asset purchase, but current evidence indicates a completed take-private transaction; exclude from active US-listed universe unless public listing status changes.

Need a later pass for private or non-US comparables in coffee extracts, cold brew concentrates, commercial roasting equipment, beverage QA/testing, and traceability software, because many likely chokepoint assets may not be US-listed.

node: Private-label coffee, tea, extracts, and beverage solutions for restaurants and foodservice
summary: Layer 1B expands the underfollowed universe for B2B coffee, tea, extracts, and beverage solutions tied to restaurants, foodservice, convenience, hospitality, and private-label programs. The strongest direct public-market fit found is Westrock Coffee, a sub-$1B integrated coffee/tea/extract solutions platform with explicit foodservice, restaurant, convenience, hospitality, private-label, and RTD exposure. Farmer Bros and Coffee Holding are much smaller, more speculative route-service/private-label coffee names with direct node relevance but balance-sheet, scale, liquidity, and customer-verification risk. Keurig Dr Pepper is included only as a reference/context anchor because it is a large-cap beverage and coffee systems company with away-from-home and fast-food fountain/coffee exposure, not an underfollowed small/mid-cap discovery name. TreeHouse Foods was relevant historically via the Farmer Brothers coffee asset acquisition, but current search evidence indicates it completed a take-private transaction and therefore should not be treated as an active US-listed candidate in this pass.
